text:
SRE-Bot: ALERT: elevated telemetry egress errors (HTTP 429) from us-central exporters to observability-collector. Affected services: prometheus-exporter, fluentd. Auto-escalation triggered. :rotating_light:
Marie: seeing blank metrics on all us-central dashboards, node autoscaler started killing pods with failed readiness checks.
Jordan: confirming, getting repeated `HTTP/2 429` from collector on outbound TLS. Packets show egress NAT reuse; looks like provider rate limiting at project level.
Luisa: opening cloud console, I can see egress rate cap on the project for collector-host:443. Raising a support case.
Anshul: note — we recently shifted inference telemetry to mirror to primary + backup collector which doubled egress in region; could have pushed us over threshold. Also cost spike risk. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Marie: immediate question — can we fallback scrapers to buffered mode or point to backup collector temporarily? Dashboards need a baseline.
Jordan: prepping a config change: set `PROM_EXPORTER_BUFFER=true` and switch fluentd output to `backup-collector.internal:4317` for namespace `inference-us-central`. Rolling patch to k8s now.
Jordan: ```
kubectl -n inference-us-central set env deploy/prom-exporter PROM_EXPORTER_BUFFER=true
kubectl -n inference-us-central set env ds/fluentd COLLECTOR_HOST=backup-collector.internal COLLECTOR_PORT=4317
kubectl -n inference-us-central rollout restart deploy/prom-exporter
kubectl -n inference-us-central rollout restart ds/fluentd
```
SRE-Bot: config patch applied to `inference-us-central` — rolling restart started (pods -> readiness checks).
Luisa: cloud support replied: provider applied temporary rate-limit because of suspected DDoS on their collector cluster. They granted a short-term uplift (2h). We need a long-term mitigation. :lock:
Anshul: instrumentation backlog item: exporter should gracefully handle 429s by 1) exponential backoff, 2) local buffering to disk for last N samples, 3) exposing a `telemetry_buffering` gauge so dashboards show buffering instead of blank data. We should prioritize this.
Jordan: agreed. I'm pushing a quick patch to exporter to catch 429 -> write payload to `/var/tmp/telemetry-buffer` and increment `telemetry_buffered_samples`. Will open PR and canary at 5%.
Marie: canary plan: 5% pods in us-central with buffered exporter and backup collector. Monitor `429_rate`, `telemetry_buffered_samples`, and dashboards for 30m. If good, promote. Creating incident ticket INC-2891.
SRE-Bot: Canary rollout complete: 5% updated, no additional 429s for canary pods. Metrics show buffered samples draining to backup collector. :white_check_mark:
Luisa: after provider uplift and canary success, I'm repointing most traffic back to primary collector but reducing scrape concurrency by 30% as a safety net.
Anshul: adding a synthetic probe that scrapes the exporter every 60s and alerts on missing samples for 2 consecutive probes. Also adding a counter for `telemetry_egress_429_total`.
Jordan: follow-ups: 1) merge exporter backpressure PR (owner Jordan), 2) update runbook with steps for egress-ratecap (owner Luisa), 3) add alert for sustained collector 429s (owner Anshul), 4) postmortem INC-2891 (owner Jordan).
Marie: thanks team. We'll keep the incident open until runbook PR merged and alerts in place. Good catch and quick response. :thumbsup:
